You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer plugin):
- file: qemu_plugin/Makefile:35
- category: hygiene
- title: libhybrid_handoff.so prerequisite list omits 3 of the 6 hybrid headers the .c includes (and the vendored qemu-plugin.h)
- detail: hybrid_handoff.c lines 5-12 include hybrid/handoff_site.h, hybrid/insn_match.h, hybrid/reg_names.h, hybrid/state_abi.h, hybrid/v_drain_policy.h, hybrid/write_mask.h, and <qemu-plugin.h>. The Makefile rule (lines 35-39) lists only state_abi.h, state_abi_check.h, insn_match.h, write_mask.h. Missing: handoff_site.h, reg_names.h, v_drain_policy.h, and include/qemu-plugin.h (the Makefile header comment at lines 5-8 even says to re-copy qemu-plugin.h on an API bump, yet a re-copy does not trigger a rebuild). Editing v_drain_policy.h (the L11 drain-policy logic is a static inline in that header, per include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h) leaves a stale libhybrid_handoff.so - the exact stale-.o failure mode already recorded in the project memory note 'Pipe swallows build exit code'. The libhotIterationLoop.so rule (line 44) likewise omits its include/qemu-plugin.h dependency.
- claimed safety: Adding prerequisites (or switching to -MMD/-MP auto-deps) changes only when make rebuilds, never what it builds; the compile command line is untouched, so the produced .so is byte-identical for a given source state.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

1	# Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
2	# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
3	# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
4	#
5	# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
6	# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
7	# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
8	# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   make            # build both
12	#   make clean
13	#
14	# Output (in this directory):
15	#   libhybrid_handoff.so    -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
16	#   libhotIterationLoop.so  -- hot inner-loop detector (`andesim profile`)
17	
18	CC ?= gcc
19	
20	GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
21	GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)
22	
23	CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
24	HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
25	# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
26	QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
27	INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
28	LDFLAGS := -shared
29	LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)
30	
31	.PHONY: all clean
32	
33	all: libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
34	
35	libhybrid_handoff.so: hybrid_handoff.c \
36	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi.h \
37	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/state_abi_check.h \
38	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/insn_match.h \
39	                     $(HYBRID_INCLUDE)/hybrid/write_mask.h
40		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(INCLUDES) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hybrid_handoff.c $(LIBS)
41	
42	# hotIterationLoop is standalone: it needs only qemu-plugin.h + glib, not
43	# HYBRID_INCLUDE.
44	libhotIterationLoop.so: hotIterationLoop.c
45		$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) -o $@ hotIterationLoop.c $(LIBS)
46	
47	clean:
48		rm -f libhybrid_handoff.so libhotIterationLoop.so
49

4

input.reason: Every factual element checks out. hybrid_handoff.c (lines 5-12) directly includes 6 hybrid headers plus <qemu-plugin.h>; the Makefile rule at qemu_plugin/Makefile:35-39 lists only state_abi.h, state_abi_check.h, insn_match.h, write_mask.h, omitting handoff_site.h, reg_names.h, v_drain_policy.h, and the vendored include/qemu-plugin.h (all four exist and are compiled in). v_drain_policy.h:42 holds the L11 drain policy as a static inline, so editing it produces a stale libhybrid_handoff.so with make reporting up-to-date -- the claimed failure mode is real. The Makefile's own header comment (lines 5-8) instructs re-copying qemu-plugin.h on an API bump, yet a re-copy triggers no rebuild. libhotIterationLoop.so (rule line 44-45) likewise omits qemu-plugin.h, which hotIterationLoop.c:23 includes. The fix is behavior-free: adding prerequisites leaves the compile commands untouched, so outputs are byte-identical for a given source state; only rebuild triggering changes. Minor note: the alternative -MMD/-MP approach would add flags and emit .d sidecar files (clean rule should then remove them), but the plain prerequisite-list fix has zero observable-behavior surface.
